label: Figure 8
title: What an opening costs and how long it takes, figure by figure, with the population each rests on
caption: The cost and time figures the plan-stage records carry, each with its population. The 2025 SHRM medians are \$1,200 per nonexecutive hire and \$10,625 per executive hire, with small organisations running six requisitions per recruiter [196](#cite:196) and filling in about 45 days [43](#cite:43). The replacement-cost median across 27 case studies is 21 percent of annual salary [180](#cite:180). Output at one autoglass company was 53 percent higher after a year than at hire [157](#cite:157); 4.1 percent of accepted entry-level offers at one telecommunications company never started [144](#cite:144); managers surveyed by a staffing firm reported a mean stay of 1.7 years after an accepted counteroffer [113](#cite:113); the default federal payment clock is 30 days from a proper invoice [202](#cite:202).
how_to_read: No row is a benchmark for any one firm. The population column says who was measured, and three rows come from a single employer or a single survey; the records that cite them say so. Read the table as the parts of a cost that an invoice does not show: what it takes to acquire a hire, what a vacancy costs while it stands, and how long the cash is out before the customer pays.

explain.text: SHRM defines it as the costs of a new hire (agency fees, job boards, referral costs, travel, relocation, recruiter pay and benefits, systems) divided by hires [196](#cite:196).

The median of 27 case studies excluding executives and physicians; only 2 of the 11 papers behind them counted indirect costs, which is why the guide treats larger multiples as a controversy [180](#cite:180).
